chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام), who said:
Amīr al-Muʾminīn (عليه السلام) said: Poverty is more adornment for the believer than the bridle-strap upon the cheek of a horse.

key_terms.خَدِّ الْفَرَسِ: the cheek of the horse; the place where the bridle appears as an adornment
key_terms.لِلْمُؤْمِنِ: for the believer; in relation to one who possesses iman

ai.seo_question: How does Imam ʿAlī (عليه السلام) describe poverty for a believer?
ai.summary: This hadith presents poverty, when borne with faith, as an adornment for the believer rather than a mark of disgrace. It highlights the spiritual dignity and beauty of patience, humility, and detachment from worldly status.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Amir Al-Momineenasws said: ‘The poverty is more of an adornment for the Momin that the harness is upon the cheek of the horse’.
en.sarwar: 22. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
Amir al-Mu’minin, Ali ibn abu Talib (a.s.) has said, ‘Poverty is more beautifying for the believers than the best decorated harness with ornament is for the head of a horse.’”
